why_the_stored_value_is_stale: 1. The card's document, CA_unemploymentRate, is written ONLY by manual pipelines (canonical / live). Nothing schedules them. The stored document dates from a manual run on 2026-03-23.

2. The scheduled monthly job did fetch Canada unemployment, but under the stat name "unemployment", so it wrote CA_unemployment — a different document that the card never reads. Even a perfectly healthy monthly schedule could never refresh the card's document. (US and UK use "unemploymentRate" and are refreshed; Australia uses "unemployment" like Canada did.)
engine_investigation.why_the_stored_value_is_also_wrong: Table 14-10-0017-01 is "Labour force characteristics by gender and detailed age group, monthly, UNADJUSTED for seasonality" (confirmed from StatCan's cube metadata). For Canada / Unemployment rate / Total - Gender / 15 years and over, February 2026 it reports exactly 6.9 — the stored value. The engine labelled it "3-month moving average, seasonally adjusted". The unadjusted series is noisy (2026: Jun 6.1, Jul 6.7, Aug 7.3, Sep 6.2) whereas the verified seasonally adjusted series (14-10-0287-01) reads Feb 6.7 ... Sep 6.5.

decision_rules_in_one_firestore_transact: StatCan reporting month NEWER than the stored month -> write (merge).
Same month, document already from the verified series -> NO write and NO audit-log entry (also not rewritten on repeat runs).
OLDER month than stored -> NO write: a missing or rolled-back release never overwrites a newer value.
Same month but stored from another series (the old unadjusted 14-10-0017-01 value) -> one corrective write, then stable.
Stored month unreadable -> write (repairs a malformed document).

StatCan unreachable, empty data, or the series identity check fails -> NO write; the stat document is never read or written and the Firestore handle is not even requested; one failure entry in data_audit_log.
scheduler_strategy.stored_month_is_read_from: latest_period (our documents), the engine's older "YYYY-MM" updated field, or a display label such as "Sep 2026".
deliberate_limits: A revision of the already-published latest month (same month, different value) is NOT rewritten; it is picked up with the next month's release, which refreshes the whole 12-month trend. This is the stated rule (only newer reporting periods update).
The manual canonical / live uploads are operator actions and do not apply the "only newer" gate (canonical also wipes the collection by design). They are protected only against stale saved files.
Operators who run the monthly tier by hand will no longer refresh Canada unemployment; they must run `npm run scheduler:ca-unemployment` after StatCan's release.

scheduler_host_findings.conclusion: NOT ESTABLISHED. The repository does not say where (or whether) the scheduler runs, and there is no evidence that a cron-driven instance is running anywhere. Pushing to GitHub does NOT activate it.
evidence: Configuration: no Dockerfile, Procfile, PM2/ecosystem file, CI workflow (.github absent), Render/Railway/Fly/Vercel/Heroku config, or deployment documentation in civic-voice-engine. firebase.json deploys only Cloud Functions from functions/ (weekly/daily aggregators), none of which writes social_stats.

What the scheduler is: `npm run scheduler` = `node src/scheduler.js`, a long-lived Node process using node-cron. It needs a machine that stays on; a bare start only registers schedules and runs nothing until their time (run-on-start is opt-in).

How it has actually been operated: civic-voice-app/docs/ENGINE_SCHEDULER_AUDIT.md §12 records an operator running tiers BY HAND (`npm run scheduler:budget-analytics`, `:weekly`, `:monthly`, `:bimonthly`, `:targeted-stats`) and checking local terminal output and Firestore scheduler_status.

what_this_means: Unless someone starts and keeps `npm run scheduler` running somewhere, none of the cron entries (including the new 15th/22nd check) will fire; the dependable way to refresh is the on-demand command.

The authoritative record of when the monthly tier last actually ran is Firestore scheduler_status/monthly.completedAt (and data_audit_log). That needs a read, which was out of scope; it is the one-step way to settle the question.
